planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; give it a raised bed or rock garden pocket where its tiny scale won't be lost.

directions: Little Gem forms a tight, flattened globe of short, twisted, densely packed medium-green needles, arising originally as a witch's broom found on 'Nidiformis' and retaining an even more diminutive scale than its parent. Growth is among the slowest of any Norway spruce cultivar, typically under an inch a year, so a specimen still reads as a miniature after a decade in the ground. Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade and avoid soggy sites, since Norway spruce roots resent standing water. No shearing is needed; simply remove any stray reverted shoot with plain green vigorous growth back to its point of origin.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; a narrow trough or the front of a rock garden shows off its slim silhouette.

directions: Compressa is an extremely narrow, upright miniature juniper that builds a dense column of blue-green, awl-shaped foliage a fraction of the width of most dwarf conifers, taking on a coppery cast through winter cold. It is prized for troughs, miniature gardens, and container groupings where its exact scale and slow, steady growth of only an inch or two a year keep proportions in check for many years. Grow in full sun in lean, sharply drained soil, since wet feet and heavy shade both cause the tight foliage to open up and thin. It needs no pruning to hold its spire-like form and tolerates drought, wind, and poor rocky soil once established.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; give it room at the front of a bed since the cushion widens faster than it rises.

directions: Slowmound builds a dense, symmetrical cushion of short, rich dark green needles, growing only a few inches a year to stay far more compact and tidy than seedling-grown mugo pine sold under that name alone. Its neat mounded habit works well as a foundation anchor, rock garden specimen, or container subject where an unpredictably sprawling mugo would quickly outgrow its space. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil; it tolerates poor, rocky, alkaline ground and windy exposure once established, and resents wet, poorly drained sites. Little pruning is required beyond an occasional candle trim in spring if an even tighter habit is wanted.

common_name: Blue Shag Dwarf Eastern White Pine

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Blue Shag is a rounded, flattened-globe selection of eastern white pine discovered as a witch's broom, holding soft, blue-green needles that are shorter and far more densely packed than the wild species. The result is a plush, touchable mound that keeps its neat symmetrical shape without shearing, making it a favorite for foundation plantings and mixed conifer borders. Grow in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, sheltered from strong winter wind and road salt, both of which can discolor the fine needles. It needs only light shaping if any, since its natural habit already stays dense and rounded for many years.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade, sheltered from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind.

directions: Tenzan is one of the smallest known Japanese cedar cultivars, forming an extremely dense, flat-topped cushion of short, tightly packed, prickly dark green needles that turn bronze-red in winter cold. Growth is measured in fractions of an inch a year, so it belongs in a trough, alpine bed, or miniature conifer collection rather than a general shrub border. Grow in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade, since Tenzan is prone to scorching in hot, direct sun and dry wind despite its cold hardiness. It needs no pruning to keep its dense bun-like form and should never be allowed to dry out completely at the root.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; a sheltered site protects the fine needles from winter burn.

directions: Jean's Dilly is a slow, dense sport of dwarf Alberta spruce selected for a naturally narrow cone shape and a low tendency to throw the coarse reverted growth that plagues many Alberta spruce plantings. It grows at only half to two-thirds the rate of ordinary dwarf Alberta spruce, holding a neat, perfectly conical form without shearing for many years. Grow in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade and site it out of harsh winter wind and reflected sun, since the fine needles are susceptible to winter burn and spider mites in hot, dry spots. Check periodically for any fast-growing green shoot reverting to the species and prune it out at its base.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; give it open exposure so the silvery-blue color develops fully.

directions: Glauca Globosa forms a dense, broadly rounded mound of stiff, sickle-shaped needles in an intense silvery blue, holding a globe shape while young before slowly developing a leading shoot with age. It is one of the most reliably compact blue spruce selections, growing only two to three inches a year and staying in scale with foundation plantings and rock gardens far longer than seedling dwarf blue spruce. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil, since full exposure keeps the needle color richest and dense shade causes thin, open growth. Prune out any upright leader if a low, mounded look is preferred, and otherwise leave it unsheared to keep its naturally soft outline.
